heading: Pune civic body plans Taljai Hill tunnel to link Sinhagad, Satara roads
author: Ajay Jadhav
paragraphs: After initiating the process to develop a road tunnel through Vetal Hill connecting Kothrud to Pashan and Aundh, the Pune Municipal Corporation (PMC) is now pushing for another tunnel through Taljai Hill to connect the Sinhagad Road area with Satara Road and reduce travel time for commuters.

“Considering the increasing traffic between Hingne Khurd on Sinhagad Road and Sahakarnagar on Satara Road, citizens are facing considerable inconvenience while commuting between the two locations,” Mayor Manjusha Nagpure said.
She said the civic body was planning to implement the long-pending proposal for a tunnel through Taljai Hill, connecting Hingne Khurd with Sahakarnagar.
“The tunnel will help resolve the traffic issue in the city,” she said.
According to the PMC administration, three road tunnels have been proposed through the city’s hills.

The proposed Taljai Hill tunnel would connect the densely populated areas of Katraj, Dhankawadi, Bibwewadi and Sahakarnagar on Satara Road with Sinhagad Road and Karvenagar, reducing travel time between the two areas, Nagpure said.

The other two proposed tunnels would pass through Vetal Hill. One, connecting Gokhalenagar with Pashan-Panchvati, is expected to help ease congestion on Ganeshkhind Road and Senapati Bapat Road. The second, from Sutardara in Kothrud to Panchvati, would connect Hingne and Kothrud with Pashan, Aundh and Baner, helping reduce traffic on Paud Road, Karve Road and Senapati Bapat Road, Nagpure added.
Nagpure said she had asked the civic administration to examine the feasibility of the Taljai Hill tunnel, which is intended to reduce both travel time and distance for commuters.
Providing alternative routes and making Pune’s transport system more efficient are among the key initiatives being pursued by the mayor.

According to civic officials, however, the construction of road tunnels through the hills would be feasible only if the project costs could be recovered by collecting tolls from four-wheelers using them.

“The PMC has already taken up the development of the High Capacity Mass Transit Route (HCMTR) and the Inner Ring Road, along with long-pending road projects such as Katraj-Kondhwa and Shivane-Kharadi, at its own expense. The tunnels are expected to be expensive, and a revenue source will therefore be required to recover the project cost,” a civic officer said.
